data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 argues against decentralization by asserting that a large service can implement 'bridge-population fail-safes' isolating redundant components behind strict boundaries, but it never engages with the problem's core requirement: identifying evidence that distinguishes truly independent failures from merely-uncorrelated-until-shared-cause failures. Its own countercondition even concedes the fail-safe itself may be a shared component that can fail (a correlated point), yet the main argument never explains how one would empirically determine whether the decentralized network's node failures are truly independent or only appear so until the shared foundational zero-day is discovered. The argument thus fails half the stated problem while also leaving its key large-service claim internally undercut by its own listed countercondition.
